title: Stratus Data - Renewal, Capacity Uplift & EU Private Onboarding Review
next_steps: Redwood to send updated 12-month committed capacity quote with burst allowance
Schedule 1-hour benchmarking run for EU private deployment w/ sample prompts (Dev + Priya)
Compile SOC2 + KMS architecture notes and share w/ Stratus security team
Legal contact exchange to begin SOW draft
action_items: Mariana Ortiz: Draft and send revised pricing spreadsheet with month-by-month commit and burst notes (due: 2026-11-24)
Dev Patel: Prepare benchmark harness and list of sample prompts, coordinate run window with Priya (due: 2026-11-26)
Priya Menon: Provide IP allowlist + VPC CIDR details for private deployment (due: 2026-11-25)
Gavin Clark: Share procurement timeline and required PO format (due: 2026-11-30)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-22 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 38 minutes | Attendees: Mariana Ortiz (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Zhou (Redwood CSM); Omar Rahman (Stratus Head of ML), Priya Menon (Infra), Gavin Clark (Procurement)
summary: Renewal and expansion check-in: Stratus plans a 12-month renewal with a 2.5x baseline capacity uplift and wants EU private deployment added. Discussed architecture requirements for VPC/on-prem style private control plane, burst capacity behavior, SLOs, and security artifacts. Agreed to run a benchmarking window in EU private env, Redwood to send updated quote and security pack, procurement to share PO timeline.
topics: Capacity uplift and committed burst modeling
EU private/VPC onboarding and network requirements
Contract extension length and commercial cadence
transcript:
[00:00] Mariana Ortiz: Alright hey everyone, thanks for joining — we can run 30–40 minutes, is that still good?
[00:05] Omar Rahman: Yeah that works, thanks. I know we have a bunch to cover — renewal numbers and the EU private plan.
[00:12] Dev Patel: Quick intro from our side, I'm Dev on the infra team, I'll lead the technical bits for the private deployment and the bench.
[00:18] Priya Menon: Hi all, Priya here. We're the infra owners; we'll own VPC peering and networking.
[00:22] Lena Zhou: Lena from CSM, I'll keep things moving on timelines and onboarding.
[00:27] Gavin Clark: Gavin from procurement, I'll be the PO contact.
[00:30] Mariana Ortiz: Great. Omar, to kick off — can you recap your top priorities for the renewal? What's driving the capacity bump?
[00:40] Omar Rahman: Sure. We launched a new summarization feature in Q3 and usage spiked — forecasts show steady growth, roughly 2.5x token volume versus our current commit. Also legal wants data residency in EU for a subset of models so we need private control plane there.
[00:55] Mariana Ortiz: OK, that maps to two asks: committed capacity uplift and EU private. Do you have a preference for how to structure the commit — big annual commit, or monthly ramp?
[01:06] Omar Rahman: We'd prefer a 12-month commitment but with monthly ramp allowances because the feature has seasonal peaks. We also want burst headroom for spikes — maybe an explicit burst pool or overage pricing cap.
[01:18] Dev Patel: Technically we can set a reserved GPU pool for Stratus in the EU region and allow burst to shared capacity with a cap. For private deployments we do a private control plane plus customer VPC peering. Priya, does that match network expectations?
[01:31] Priya Menon: Yes. We'll need specific CIDR ranges and IP allowlists. Also KMS integration is required — keys must be customer-managed. Can Redwood support HSM/KMS rotation and CMK?
[01:43] Dev Patel: Yes, we support KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) and HSM-backed modules in the Private offering. We'll capture the KMS flow in the security doc.
[01:50] Priya Menon: Good. Also latency: our internal SLO is 250ms p95 for short completions; can Redwood sustain that in private EU?
[01:59] Dev Patel: Our Dedicated/Private configs can meet p95 in the 150–300ms range depending on model family and sequence length. For summarization with average seq length of ~600 tokens we should aim for 220–300ms p95; bench run will confirm.
[02:13] Omar Rahman: Bench results are critical — legal and product want measured numbers before signoff.
[02:18] Mariana Ortiz: Absolutely — action: we schedule a dedicated benchmark in your EU private environment. Dev, can you outline what you'll need?
[02:25] Dev Patel: Sample prompts, expected QPS, traffic pattern, typical sequence length, and a window for running the test. Ideally a 4-hour run to capture warm cache behavior and cold start scenarios.
[02:34] Priya Menon: We'll provide prompts and sample traffic. One note: we have intermittent peak at 3:00 AM UTC — global batch runs — so the bench should include a high-burst period.
[02:44] Gavin Clark: For procurement, quick question on billing: do you do monthly invoices against committed spend with overage reconciliation? We need that spelled out for finance.
[02:53] Mariana Ortiz: Yes, we can invoice monthly against the committed baseline, and overage either billed monthly or consumed against a prepaid burst bucket depending on the commercial arrangement. We'll put both options in the quote.
[03:03] Lena Zhou: Also adding: we'll include a runbook for failover — how traffic shifts if the EU pool is saturated and fallback to other regions or smaller models occurs.
[03:12] Omar Rahman: On fallback, product allowed a controlled fallback to hosted variants in restricted cases; legal wants to avoid cross-border data movement for EU-resident requests. We need to ensure data doesn't leave EU for those tenant IDs.
[03:25] Dev Patel: Understood. We can pin model variants and enforce routing policies by tenant ID so EU-resident traffic stays in EU-only pools. We'll document that and include rate-limiting rules.
[03:36] Priya Menon: Can you also share auditing detail — are audit logs delivered into our SIEM, retention options, and can we push to our bucket?
[03:44] Dev Patel: We support streaming audit logs to customer-owned buckets and SIEM via webhook; retention is configurable in the private control plane.
[03:51] Gavin Clark: What's typical lead time to provision a private EU pod with the dedicated GPU pool?
[03:58] Mariana Ortiz: For Private deployments we usually see 4–6 weeks for initial provisioning and networking, shorter if we schedule in an available capacity window. We'll include a provisioning schedule in the SOW.
[04:08] Omar Rahman: Cost-wise, the big ask is to keep per-token economics reasonable as we scale. We don't want a linear 2.5x cost increase for 2.5x usage. Any flex on tiered pricing?
[04:19] Mariana Ortiz: We can model a tiered commit that reduces per-token price as you pass volume thresholds, plus a burst pool that's priced differently. I'll put three scenarios in the updated quote: conservative ramp, steady growth commit, and aggressive uplift with discounts.
[04:31] Priya Menon: Do you have references for other EU private customers to confirm performance and compliance posture?
[04:36] Lena Zhou: We have a redacted case study and contact reference we can share; I'll include that in the security pack.
[04:43] Omar Rahman: On encryption: we need end-to-end at rest, and ephemeral keys during inference lifecycle. Are model weights ever exposed outside the private pool?
[04:54] Dev Patel: Model weights live on the private nodes for the EU private offering. We don't egress weights. We'll detail disk encryption and ephemeral cache flush policies.
[05:02] Gavin Clark: Legal will want the SLA guarantees — uptime and latency. Can you commit to a latency SLA or only uptime + targets?
[05:12] Mariana Ortiz: We offer uptime SLAs for Dedicated/Private and latency targets with credits tied to rolling averages. For strict latency SLAs we usually define service credits based on p95 thresholds in the SOW; we'll propose an approach.
[05:23] Omar Rahman: Ok. Timeline wise, we want to close the contract by end of December and have EU private live by end of January if possible. Is that realistic?
[05:33] Mariana Ortiz: It's tight but feasible — procurement and legal cycles matter. If we start the SOW drafting this week and run the benchmarks next week, provisioning could begin early January.
[05:43] Gavin Clark: We'll need SSO/SAML integration notes and RBAC details too.
[05:48] Dev Patel: We'll share an integration guide for SSO and RBAC, and sample IAM roles for the private control plane.
[05:55] Lena Zhou: I'll also include an onboarding checklist and estimated dates per milestone.
[06:00] Omar Rahman: One more question: we have an internal vector DB coupling (3rd party), will Redwood support affinities like colocating model routing closer to our DB for lower hop latency?
[06:12] Dev Patel: We can suggest network placement and dedicated peering to reduce hops; colocating in the same region and direct peering will help. We'll include network topology recommendations in the tech notes.
[06:22] Priya Menon: For the bench — what metrics will you collect? We need p50/p95/p99, token cost per request, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and cold-start frequencies.
[06:33] Dev Patel: Yep, we'll capture those: latency percentiles, throughput, tokenized cost, GPU and memory utilization, KV cache hit/miss, and tail latency distribution. We will share raw logs and a summary dashboard.
[06:44] Mariana Ortiz: Great. Any competitors in the conversation internally? Stratus mentioned evaluating a couple options earlier — Omar?
[06:50] Omar Rahman: We did a short bake-off with Bedrock and Anthropic earlier this quarter; Bedrock looked cheaper initially but didn't have the private deployment patterns we need. Anthropic's latency profile was OK but pricing was higher at scale.
[07:03] Mariana Ortiz: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood's private offering and pricing tiers map against those.
[07:09] Gavin Clark: On legal, are there standard indemnities and data clauses or do we expect heavy negotiation?
[07:16] Mariana Ortiz: We use a standard enterprise template we can start from; larger customers add a couple clauses but usually it's straightforward. We can share the template with redactions.
[07:24] Priya Menon: Anything else from your side?
[07:27] Omar Rahman: No, that covers it. We'll want the bench and quote to be the main artifacts.
[07:32] Mariana Ortiz: Excellent. Recap — Redwood sends updated quote + commercial scenarios, security pack (SOC2, KMS, audit), and schedule the EU private bench. Stratus to send prompts, network CIDR, and procurement timeline. We'll follow up with an SOW kickoff.
[07:45] Lena Zhou: I'll create a shared folder with artifacts and a proposed calendar invite for the bench window; watch for that from me.
[07:52] Gavin Clark: Expect a procurement note by end of week.
[07:55] Mariana Ortiz: Thanks everyone. We'll target those deliverables this week. Appreciate your time.
[08:01] [meeting ends]
